Median and inter-quartile range across 11 repetitions of 2000000 iterations each, after discarding a warm-up repetition. Every measured value is held live with an inline-asm optimisation barrier, so the computation is not deleted as dead code.

`tsc_now` is an upper bound, not an isolated cost. An empty barrier-only loop runs at 0.313 ns/iteration, which is within noise of the counter-read loop itself: the read issues alongside the loop's own work rather than serialising with it, so the two are not separable in throughput mode.

### Cache-line padding A/B

| queue layout | M ops/s |
|---|---:|
| padded (cache-line separated) | 26.9 |
| unpadded (false sharing) | 112.7 |

On this machine the **unpadded** layout is 4.19x faster. The two queues are identical apart from the `alignas` on the cursors — including the cached opposite-cursor snapshots, without which the comparison measures two differences at once.

Measured with a 128-byte cache line on a machine with 10 hardware threads, pinning: no. This result is a property of a cache topology, not of the code, and it is measured on AArch64 only. It should not be generalised to x86 without an x86 run.
